record.title: A paper proposes auditability as a fourth machine-unlearning criterion and reports a two-stage method with dataset tradeoffs
record.summary: The Nov. 4 arXiv preprint “Widen the Gap, Hide the Gap” treats auditability—whether a provider can distinguish requested-forget examples from retained examples under a chosen statistic—as a fourth criterion for machine unlearning. It proposes GapWiden, which trains an audit-statistic gap into the unlearned model, and GapVeil, an inference-time rejection sampler intended to reduce disclosure of that gap. The authors report evaluations over eleven unlearning methods on TOFU and MUSE. Results are paper-reported: auditability rises toward 0.99 on MUSE, but retain performance on MUSE News falls from 0.569 to 0.380. These benchmark results do not establish deletion from a deployed model or proof of deletion for an individual request.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper defines unlearning auditability as a statistic that separates requested-forget examples from retained examples, and proposes the GapWiden training stage plus the GapVeil inference-time rejection sampler.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across eleven unlearning methods on TOFU and MUSE, the authors report that their two-stage procedure improves auditability and leakage metrics; reported outcomes vary across datasets and methods.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On MUSE News, the paper reports that retain performance decreases from 0.569 to 0.380 with the proposed procedure, which the authors attribute to overlap between forget and retain content.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The benchmark results do not establish deletion from deployed systems, compliance with an individual deletion request, or an operationally reliable user-facing deletion certificate.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the reported TOFU/MUSE evaluation was performed; underlying baselines and audit/leakage metrics remain author-reported.

The paper formalizes a benchmark statistic, not a production deletion procedure or an individual-request certificate; it does not establish that trained information has been removed across prompts or deployment pathways.
Retain utility degrades materially on MUSE News, and the compute/latency cost of GapWiden retraining and repeated rejection sampling is not characterized here as a production tradeoff.
The authors state that standardized consensus criteria for demonstrable unlearning remain unresolved; the proposed audit statistic is one operational definition.

brief.importance_rationale: If a model provider can separately demonstrate removal while limiting inference-time disclosure, unlearning audits could become more useful for deletion accountability. The paper reports benchmark results on TOFU and MUSE, but its own MUSE News result shows a substantial retain-performance tradeoff; no deployed deletion process or independent reproduction is established.
limitations: All empirical results are author-reported; no independent reproduction was performed.
TOFU and MUSE benchmark results do not demonstrate deployed-model erasure, regulatory compliance or an individual user deletion certificate.
MUSE News retain performance falls from 0.569 to 0.380 in the reported result; tradeoffs differ across datasets.
The authors describe auditability as a starting operational definition and identify consensus criteria as unresolved.
Membership leakage metrics and the rejection sampler’s production latency/cost have not been independently validated here.
brief.summary: The Nov. 4 arXiv preprint “Widen the Gap, Hide the Gap” treats auditability—whether a provider can distinguish requested-forget examples from retained examples under a chosen statistic—as a fourth criterion for machine unlearning. It proposes GapWiden, which trains an audit-statistic gap into the unlearned model, and GapVeil, an inference-time rejection sampler intended to reduce disclosure of that gap. The authors report evaluations over eleven unlearning methods on TOFU and MUSE. Results are paper-reported: auditability rises toward 0.99 on MUSE, but retain performance on MUSE News falls from 0.569 to 0.380. These benchmark results do not establish deletion from a deployed model or proof of deletion for an individual request.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report auditability near 0.99 on MUSE and improvements on several other metrics, with dataset- and method-dependent retain/forget tradeoffs. MUSE News retain score declines 0.569→0.380.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv v1 paper and appendix contain the stated method, benchmarks and reported results. the research desk verified the publication and inspected the paper; it did not reproduce the results or validate real-world deletion.
technical.mechanism: GapWiden adds an optimization stage that increases the base-versus-unlearned log-probability gap on forget examples while anchoring the gap near zero on retain examples. GapVeil then samples from the base model with rejection criteria based on those audit statistics, with rejected content tokens suppressed in subsequent proposals.
technical.regime: Paper-reported experiments over eleven unlearning methods; TOFU uses Llama 3.2 1B/3B and Llama 3.1 8B variants, and MUSE uses Llama 2 7B on News and Books.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares each method with and without the proposed stages and includes a retrained oracle benchmark; these are author-run evaluations, not an independent matched reproduction.

brief.title: A paper proposes auditability as a fourth machine-unlearning criterion and reports a two-stage method with dataset tradeoffs
brief.why_it_matters: A deletion workflow needs evidence that requested material was removed, while an observable audit signal can itself reveal membership. The paper makes that tension an explicit evaluation target and tests a training-plus-decoding approach. Its dataset-specific retain tradeoff and unverified operational assumptions matter before treating auditability as a practical guarantee.
